text: Type one sentence, get a finished video.
That's how AI video gets sold.
But generation is the smallest part. The teams
who do this well spend most of the
work before a single frame exists.
First, research. Dozens of searches across forums,
papers and news, so every number in
the script traces back to a source.
Then the script, words budgeted against
seconds, and a scene plan for
what you see at each moment.
Then the assets: narration, images, music. Each
job routed to the best available tool,
and every choice written down.
Then the cut, camera moves, captions, a
mix. And only then the render, the
part everyone assumes is the whole job.
The last step is invisible. The agent audits
its own film, frame by frame, and refuses
to ship it if it fails.
That's not generation. That's production.
OpenMontage, twelve pipelines, one agent.
